title: Carbon Emissions, Mutual Fund Trading, and the Liquidity of Corporate Bonds
eligible_reason: Single adoption date. Every DiD specification interacts a carbon-exposure measure with one common post indicator: the Paris Agreement (2015Q4, q == 56; monthly mt 631-636) in Tables 3, 5, 7, 12A and A4, or the 2016 election (2016Q4, q == 60) in Tables 8, 9, 12B, in symmetric 4-quarter / 6-month windows with the event period dropped. The exposure measure is continuous at the fund level (fundcarbon_raw_vw, Tables 3 and 8) and a binary high-carbon dummy at the bond level (carbon_rank1); all treated units switch at the same date, so there are no staggered cohorts. Baseline Tables 2, 4, 6, 11 regress outcomes on the carbon measure without any post indicator. Every column also includes time-varying fund or bond controls.
design_notes: Three panels: fund-month flow_panel.dta (Tables 2-3, 8), bond-quarter quarter_panel.dta (Tables 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, 12, A3-A4, IA1-IA3), bond-fund-quarter bond_fund_panel.dta (Table 6). Table 5 (quarter_panel.do lines 17-39): keep q 52-60, drop q 56, In = 1 for q 57-60, esg_in = carbon_rank1 x In; reghdfe prop_mut_change esg_in carbon_rank1 + controls, absorb(cusip_id q), cluster(cusip_id q). Table 3 (flow_panel.do lines 17-30): mt 624-636, drop 630, esg_in = fundcarbon_raw_vw x In, absorb(mt lipper_class crsp_portno). Table 9 / Table 8: same around 2016Q4 (esg_after). Table 7 adds oil exposure interaction. Table 11-12: liquidity outcomes (am_illiq, roll2, irc_illiq) with high/low mutual-fund-ownership subsamples. Table 10 and Figure 2 in SAS.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One event date per analysis (Paris Agreement 2015Q4; election 2016Q4).

specs.exclusion_reason: single adoption date (Paris Agreement 2015Q4); time-varying bond controls
specs.outcome: prop_mut_change (change in mutual fund ownership, x100)
specs.treatment_var: esg_in (= carbon_rank1 x In) with carbon_rank1 main effect
specs.treatment_definition: carbon_rank1 = high-carbon issuer dummy; In = 1 for 2016Q1-2016Q4 (q 57-60), 0 for 2014Q4-2015Q3 (q 52-55); q 56 dropped
specs.controls: rating ttm age (col 2); + logme logbm ivol hold numest (col 3); col 1 adds coupon b_size
specs.data_file: data/quarter_panel.dta (NOT shipped; quarter_panel_pseudo.dta is pseudo data)
specs.notes: Column 4 adds pre-trend interactions esg_prepa3 esg_prepa2.

specs.exclusion_reason: single adoption date; continuous exposure (fundcarbon_raw_vw); fund controls in col 3
specs.treatment_var: esg_in (= fundcarbon_raw_vw x In) with fundcarbon_raw_vw main effect
specs.treatment_definition: fundcarbon_raw_vw = value-weighted carbon exposure of the fund's bond portfolio (continuous); In = 1 for mt 631-636 (post Paris), 0 for mt 624-629
after = 1 for q 61-64, 0 for q 56-59; q 60 dropped
specs.controls: rating ttm age (+ logme logbm ivol hold numest)
specs.notes: Tables 12A/12B repeat for liquidity outcomes on high-ownership bonds.

data_access_note: README: 'Due to license restrictions, the pseudo data with the same data structure (same dataset name with pseudo as the suffix) are provided for illustration. They cannot be used to generate the results.' Sources: CRSP mutual funds, eMAXX holdings, TRACE, FISD, MSCI ESG, Compustat/CRSP/13f/IBES (all licensed via WRDS or Refinitiv).
software_notes: Stata/MP 15.1 (reghdfe, eststo/esttab) and SAS 9.4 (Table 1, Table 10, Table A1).
screener_notes: Screened from package only. Candidate flag cites Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess, but the code contains no modern estimator; the single-event design makes the question moot.
